account:
Today has mostly appeared routine: market trade, accounts, and tea with the neighbour. The unusual thing is a repeated, vague rumor about a bridge or port change. I heard Townsfolk 03 and 23 mention it, and the neighbour has also heard it without specifics. The secretary traced the inn's version to Townsfolk 03; the innkeeper denies proposing or announcing a change. Builder reports the bridge passable and no confirmed defects. Freight reportedly found undamaged roads and a trouble-free ferry crossing, and is offering deliveries, storage and ferry service. None of that establishes a planned change or explains the rumor's purpose.

The baker reports ordinary bread sales and no special celebration. The neighbour says riverside life is peaceful and has personally seen nothing unusual. Builder has repeatedly asked about repair work, but has accepted that any actual need requires an estimate and approval. I have authorized no repair spending, and the secretary's accounts record confirms no receipts, claims or contracts today.

I suspect there may be informal talk circulating beyond my knowledge, but I have no evidence of a secret gathering, coordinated scheme, or ulterior purpose. Finding out directly what Townsfolk 03 actually heard, and from whom, would be more useful than treating repetition as confirmation. I am now back in my office with the secretary, reviewing the afternoon records; another book has just been placed in the appointments chest.
